newsitem.title: USA: Brooks & Dunn duo win top country music award.
newsitem.headline: Brooks & Dunn duo win top country music award.

text.p: Kix Brooks and Ronnie Dunn, known to country music fans as Brooks and Dunn, on Wednesday night won the top award, Entertainer of the Year, at the 30th annual Country Music Association Awards show.
The two, the best-selling duo in country music history, also were named Duo of the Year for the fifth consecutive year. It was the first time a duo has been named Entertainer of the Year.

Texas singer George Strait, twice a CMA Entertainer of the Year at earlier awards shows, won his first Single of the Year award with the popular "Check Yes or No," as well as winning for Album of the Year and Male Vocalist of the Year.

Singer-songwriter Vince Gill, who hosted the live awards show on CBS, won Song of the Year for his gospel-themed "Go Rest High on That Mountain," and he and singer-actress Dolly Parton shared the award for Vocal Event of the Year on Parton's composition, "I Will Always Love You."
Gill's two awards -- he has won more CMA awards than any other performer -- brought his career total to 17.
Patty Loveless, who won the CMA honour for Album of the Year in 1995, this time won Female Vocalist of the Year.

The Mavericks, a former Miami-based group with Hispanic roots, was named Vocal Group of the Year for the second year running. Guitarist-singer Junior Brown won the Music Video of the Year title and 22-year-old Bryan White won the Horizon award for the most promising performer.
Fiddler Mark O'Connor took home the Musician of the Year award for the sixth time.
LeAnn Rimes, at 14 the youngest CMA nominee in the show's history, was nominated for the Horizon award and for Single of the Year because of her Patsy Cline-like song, "Blue."

She won neither, but opened the nationally televised show at the Grand Ole Opry House by singing her hit. Later, she also sang the yodeling hit of the late Patsy Montana, "I Want to Be a Cowboy's Sweetheart" during the segment honouring Montana's induction into the Country Music Hall of Fame.
Singer-songwriter-actor Kris Kristofferson introduced Ray Price, another Hall of Fame inductee, and the two performed Kristofferson's hit, "For the Good Times," which became Price's signature song.
Buck Owens, who hosted television's long-running "Heehaw" show, was the third star named to the Hall of Fame.
Backstage after the awards show, Gill explained why he had been so overcome with emotion on receipt of the Song of the Year award -- he was only able to choke out "thanks."
He wrote the song after the death of singer Keith Whitley, he said, but did not finish it until some time later when his own brother died suddenly.
